# Architecture

_Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made._

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, eight storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with both EU and US each split into two storefronts (domestic + international).

## Pre-Build Decisions

These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

| #   | Decision                     | Status                                 |
| --- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Browser & device matrix      | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
| 2   | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending       |
| 3   | Performance budgets          | ✅ Confirmed (informal)                |
| 4   | Client-side error reporting  | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool             |
| 5   | Feature-flag tool            | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
| 6   | Translation fallback chain   | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending       |

### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅

**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.

### #2 — Accessibility 🟡

**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.

### #3 — Performance budgets ✅

**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.

### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡

[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:

| Content type | Suggested chain          | Why                                          |
| ------------ | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| UI strings   | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning                            |
| Editorial    | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages                  |
| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |

REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.

### Accepted risks

**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.

**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.

## Frontend Stack

### Bundled by PWA Kit

| Layer                        | Library                                               | Notes                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base framework               | PWA Kit v3+                                           | Salesforce storefront foundation                                                      |
| UI framework                 | React 18 + Chakra UI                                  | Component library + theme system                                                      |
| Routing                      | React Router v6                                       |                                                                                       |
| Server/async state           | TanStack Query (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) | All SFCC data fetching                                                                |
| i18n                         | react-intl                                            | Translations in `translations/`                                                       |
| Build + dev server           | Webpack 5 (via `pwa-kit-dev`)                         |                                                                                       |
| Build + test runner (legacy) | Jest (via `pwa-kit-dev test`)                         | `jest.config.js` — kept for PWA Kit internals; superseded by Vitest for project tests |

### Project additions

| Layer                                  | Library                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Type safety                            | TypeScript strict mode                         | `tsconfig.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8                                    | `storybook dev -p 6006`; `play` functions are the primary tool for component-level interaction testing                                                                                                              |
| Storybook a11y addon                   | `@storybook/addon-a11y`                        | Component-level accessibility checks during development and in Storybook test runs                                                                                                                                  |
| Unit test runner                       | Vitest                                         | `vitest.config.ts`; replaces `pwa-kit-dev test` for project tests                                                                                                                                                   |
| Accessibility testing                  | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers; see Pre-Build Decisions #2 for outstanding items                                                                                                                      |
| E2E tests (planned)                    | Playwright                                     | Not yet configured                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Forms + validation                     | react-hook-form + zod                          | Not yet installed; add when checkout/account work begins                                                                                                                                                            |
| Global UI state                        | Zustand                                        | For shared state that outgrows Context (multi-step flows, drawer state, etc.). **SSR note:** initialise store per-request — never as a module singleton — to prevent state leaking across server-rendered requests. |

### External services

Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.

## Environments

Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.

**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.

**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.

## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)

Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

## Overrides Pattern

All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.

**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.

**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:

1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

## New vs. Override Components

- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.

## Key Paths

- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); per-component overrides live one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2). Register a new component override in `components/index.ts`.
- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`

## Design Source of Truth

Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.

Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.

## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)

Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.

**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.

**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread _after_ `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.

**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.

**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.

## Contentful Content Type Management

Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.

**Key paths:**

- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)

**To register a new content type:**

1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`

**To run the sync:**

```
npm run sync:contentful
```

Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account — in `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold it, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running the sync). Get the token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.

The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).

**Relationship to the React component:**
Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.

**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

## Path Aliases

Configured in four places (keep in sync):

- `babel.config.js` — `babel-plugin-module-resolver` (covers `npm start` dev server + `npm run build`)
- `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` + `paths` (TypeScript / VS Code intellisense)
- `.storybook/main.js` — `webpackFinal` alias
- `jest.config.js` — `moduleNameMapper` (PWA Kit internals)
- `vitest.config.ts` — `resolve.alias` (project tests)

| Alias | Resolves to     |
| ----- | --------------- |
| `~`   | project root    |
| `app` | `overrides/app` |

## Integration Map

All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.

**Boundary key:**

- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

| System                               | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Boundary                                                                                                                                                                                      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC)** | Storefront, product catalogue, order management (record of truth), customer accounts, Business Manager config                                                                                                                                                                                   | —                                                                                                                                                                                             | Domestic checkout owner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **MuleSoft**                         | Middleware / integration layer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | SFCC → MuleSoft + MRT-mediated (direct PWA → MuleSoft calls)                                                                                                                                  | All SFCC ↔ OMS, SFCC ↔ Omneo, SFCC ↔ Narvar calls go via MuleSoft. Select PWA operations also call MuleSoft directly via the MRT proxy layer (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) with credentials held as MRT environment variables                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **NewStore OMS**                     | Order management system, carrier selection, dispatch, label generation, boutique inventory; **system of record for order history** (no Magento order history is migrated — DMU-007/008)                                                                                                         | SFCC → MuleSoft (writes) + MRT-mediated (reads)                                                                                                                                               | **Write path (SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order creation, fulfilment, BOPIS. **Read path (MRT → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order history (CRM-056–057), order details (CRM-071–072), boutique / BOPIS stock check (CFD-043), real-time stock availability. SFCC is not in the read path. The customer-identification mechanism on the read path is **unconfirmed** (open item) — either MRT forwards the customer's SLAS JWT for MuleSoft to validate, or MRT passes the customer ID as a request parameter; whichever is agreed must prevent retrieval of an arbitrary customer's data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **AP21**                             | Retail Rewards (loyalty/VIP), product master, composition/material data; **source of product and pricing master data**                                                                                                                                                                          | SFCC → MuleSoft                                                                                                                                                                               | Real-time AP21 call at login for Retail Rewards balance; used for HS codes via Avalara. **Product and pricing feed** flows inbound AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC to populate the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks the PWA reads via SCAPI; feed cadence and exact field set TBC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Omneo**                            | CRM sync layer / system of record for customer identity and loyalty                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | SFCC → MuleSoft                                                                                                                                                                               | SFCC ↔ Omneo via MuleSoft; Omneo → Emarsys for marketing emails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Emarsys**                          | Email marketing platform                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Out-of-band                                                                                                                                                                                   | Receives opt-in/opt-out from Omneo; sends welcome and marketing emails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Adyen**                            | Payment processing (all domestic storefronts)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | SFCC (cartridge) + PWA-direct (Drop-in / Components SDK at checkout)                                                                                                                          | Credit/debit, PayPal, saved cards (tokens only). Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna targeting August 2026. Adyen Web Drop-in loads in the browser at checkout for tokenisation and 3DS2 challenges. As payment processing is strictly necessary (contractual necessity, not analytics/marketing tracking), the Drop-in is **not** Didomi consent-gated — it loads at the payment step regardless of consent choices. The fail-closed consent rule applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not to the payment flow.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Global-e**                         | International checkout owner (HK, ME, all international orders) + server-side pricing/catalogue feed into SFCC                                                                                                                                                                                  | PWA-direct (iframe embed at checkout) + SFCC server-side (pricing/catalogue feed)                                                                                                             | (1) **Iframe embed at checkout** — Global-e hosted checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route (not a full-page redirect). SFCC sends complete cart in target currency at handoff. CSP `frame-src` must allowlist the Global-e origin. (2) Server-side feed — nightly FX rates / coefficients / rounding rules from Global-e generate Global-e-market pricebooks in SFCC (PRC-34..43); daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue CSV via SFTP (PRC-54); GiveX validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44). REG-041 confirmed; PRC-34..43 final sign-off pending.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Booxi**                            | Boutique appointment booking (My Account → appointment history; CRM-165–167)                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi)                                                                                                                                                              | **Not a MuleSoft path** — the PWA calls Booxi directly from the MRT Node layer; SFCC and MuleSoft are not involved. Booxi credentials held as MRT environment variables. Previously referred to as "Booksy" in older notes — Booxi is the correct vendor. Scope still TBC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **Narvar**                           | EDD at checkout (Promise widget, formerly CONVERT), domestic order confirmation emails, shipping confirmation, tracking portal, returns portal                                                                                                                                                  | SFCC → MuleSoft (backend); PWA-direct (Promise widget)                                                                                                                                        | Narvar is NOT used for international orders (Global-e owns those)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)

Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

## Blast-Radius Mitigation

Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.

The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

```ts
import { Pool } from 'undici';

// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
  timeout: 8000,
});

// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
    dispatcher: checkoutPool, // Safely isolated!
  });
}
```

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool                   | Origin                                                                                                            | Calls                                                                           | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- | ---------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sfcc-scapi`           | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`                                                            | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password)             | 5   | 5 s              | 8 s           | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools.                                                                                                  |
| `sfcc-payments`        | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR                              | 10  | 5 s              | 8 s           | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections.                                                                                               |
| `mulesoft`             | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`                                                                                               | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20  | 5 s              | 10 s          | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange                               | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections.                                                                                                           |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`                                                                 | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password)                      | 5   | 5 s              | 15 s          | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load.                                                                                                                                                |
| `google-places`        | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New)                                                                | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059)                    | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly.                                                                                                                      |
| `booxi`                | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team)                                                              | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167)                           | 5   | 3 s              | 5 s           | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). - Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).

SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.

1	# PWA Integration Design Documents
2	
3	These documents describe each external system that the Zimmermann PWA storefront interacts with **from the PWA layer** — either browser-direct or proxied through the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer. Each system has its own document covering purpose, scope, browser-side architecture, authentication, data exchange, consent gating, performance, multi-region behaviour, graceful degradation, security and privacy, and the open items requiring client input before implementation.
4	
5	> **Scope.** PWA-layer only (browser-direct and MRT-proxied). Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here.
6	
7	The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.
8	
9	### Commerce backbone
10	
11	The data sources every storefront page depends on.
12	
13	| #   | System                                | Purpose                                                                | Document                             |
14	| --- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
15	| 1   | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders.               | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md)             |
16	| 2   | **Contentful**                        | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |
17	
18	### Account and customer data
19	
20	Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.
21	
22	| #   | System                          | Purpose                                                                                        | Document                         |
23	| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
24	| 3   | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy.                  | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
25	| 4   | **Omneo**                       | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account.                                                | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md)       |
26	| 5   | **GiveX (balance check)**       | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX.                                 | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md)       |
27	| 6   | **Booxi**                       | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md)       |
28	
29	### Checkout cluster
30	
31	The buying flow.
32	
33	| #   | System                            | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
34	| --- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
35	| 7   | **Adyen**                         | Browser-side payment Drop-in for SFCC-owned domestic checkout.                                   | [07-adyen.md](07-adyen.md)             |
36	| 8   | **Global-e**                      | International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US international).                             | [08-global-e.md](08-global-e.md)       |
37	| 9   | **Google Maps Platform (Places)** | Address autocomplete at checkout, MRT-proxied.                                                   | [09-google-maps.md](09-google-maps.md) |
38	| 10  | **Google reCAPTCHA**              | Bot protection on register / login forms — browser loads script, MRT verifies token server-side. | [10-recaptcha.md](10-recaptcha.md)     |
39	| 11  | **Narvar**                        | Estimated Delivery Date widget at checkout, domestic only.                                       | [11-narvar.md](11-narvar.md)           |
40	
41	### Cross-cutting overlays
42	
43	Consent, analytics, and customer service — applied across every page rather than tied to a specific journey.
44	
45	| #   | System                 | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
46	| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
47	| 12  | **Didomi**             | Consent Management Platform — gatekeeper for every browser-loaded third-party script.            | [12-didomi.md](12-didomi.md)           |
48	| 13  | **Google Tag Manager** | Data layer, Consent Mode v2, downstream tag orchestration via Tell No Lies.                      | [13-gtm.md](13-gtm.md)                 |
49	| 14  | **Inside Chat**        | Customer-service chat widget.                                                                    | [14-inside-chat.md](14-inside-chat.md) |
50	| 15  | **Optimizely Web**     | A/B testing and personalisation — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                           | [15-optimizely.md](15-optimizely.md)   |
51	| 16  | **Crazy Egg**          | Heatmaps and session recording — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                            | [16-crazyegg.md](16-crazyegg.md)       |
52	| 17  | **Measmerize**         | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP.                                                 | [17-measmerize.md](17-measmerize.md)   |
53	| 18  | **Vimeo**              | Product video (PDP gallery) and editorial video (homepage and content pages via Contentful CMS). | [18-vimeo.md](18-vimeo.md)             |
54	
55	## Note on runtime load order
56	
57	The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. At runtime, **Didomi loads first** (document 11) because every other browser-loaded third-party script — GTM, Inside Chat, the Narvar widget, the Google Maps proxy call, and the Adyen Drop-in — is gated by Didomi consent. Each integration document records its own consent posture; the Didomi document is the single contract that all the others honour.
58	
59	## Cross-cutting principles
60	
61	- **Fail closed on consent.** If Didomi cannot determine consent state, no third-party tracking or marketing script loads.
62	- **Fail independently.** One vendor outage must not break the storefront — each integration has a documented degradation path.
63	- **LCP budget is ≤ 2.0 s at p75 mobile.** Any browser-loaded third-party script defers behind consent or hydration and does not block first paint.
64	- **Multi-region.** Eight SFCC sites across six regions, eleven active locales. Every integration that varies by region documents the per-storefront configuration matrix.
65	- **No secrets in the browser bundle.** Public and publishable keys only — anything that grants write access lives server-side, either in MRT environment variables or in SFCC Business Manager.
66	
67	## Document template
68	
69	Each integration document follows the same structure for ease of review:
70	
71	1. Purpose and scope
72	2. Vendor relationship
73	3. Browser-side architecture
74	4. Authentication and credentials
75	5. Data exchanged
76	6. Consent and gating
77	7. Performance and loading strategy
78	8. Multi-region behaviour
79	9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
80	10. Security and privacy
81	11. Open items requiring client confirmation
82	
83	Sections may merge where the surface is narrow (for example, the GiveX document folds observability into the security and privacy section) or removed when not applicable.

Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here.

The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.

### Commerce backbone

The data sources every storefront page depends on.

| #   | System                                | Purpose                                                                | Document                             |
| --- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 1   | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders.               | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md)             |
| 2   | **Contentful**                        | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |

### Account and customer data

Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.

| #   | System                          | Purpose                                                                                        | Document                         |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 3   | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy.                  | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
| 4   | **Omneo**                       | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account.                                                | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md)       |
| 5   | **GiveX (balance check)**       | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX.                                 | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md)       |
| 6   | **Booxi**                       | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md)       |

### Checkout cluster

The buying flow.

| #   | System                            | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 7   | **Adyen**                         | Browser-side payment Drop-in for SFCC-owned domestic checkout.                                   | [07-adyen.md](07-adyen.md)             |
| 8   | **Global-e**                      | International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US international).                             | [08-global-e.md](08-global-e.md)       |
| 9   | **Google Maps Platform (Places)** | Address autocomplete at checkout, MRT-proxied.                                                   | [09-google-maps.md](09-google-maps.md) |
| 10  | **Google reCAPTCHA**              | Bot protection on register / login forms — browser loads script, MRT verifies token server-side. | [10-recaptcha.md](10-recaptcha.md)     |
| 11  | **Narvar**                        | Estimated Delivery Date widget at checkout, domestic only.                                       | [11-narvar.md](11-narvar.md)           |

### Cross-cutting overlays

Consent, analytics, and customer service — applied across every page rather than tied to a specific journey.

| #   | System                 | Purpose                                                                                          | Document                               |
| --- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| 12  | **Didomi**             | Consent Management Platform — gatekeeper for every browser-loaded third-party script.            | [12-didomi.md](12-didomi.md)           |
| 13  | **Google Tag Manager** | Data layer, Consent Mode v2, downstream tag orchestration via Tell No Lies.                      | [13-gtm.md](13-gtm.md)                 |
| 14  | **Inside Chat**        | Customer-service chat widget.                                                                    | [14-inside-chat.md](14-inside-chat.md) |
| 15  | **Optimizely Web**     | A/B testing and personalisation — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                           | [15-optimizely.md](15-optimizely.md)   |
| 16  | **Crazy Egg**          | Heatmaps and session recording — frontend-direct script (not in GTM).                            | [16-crazyegg.md](16-crazyegg.md)       |
| 17  | **Measmerize**         | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP.                                                 | [17-measmerize.md](17-measmerize.md)   |
| 18  | **Vimeo**              | Product video (PDP gallery) and editorial video (homepage and content pages via Contentful CMS). | [18-vimeo.md](18-vimeo.md)             |

## Note on runtime load order

The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. At runtime, **Didomi loads first** (document 11) because every other browser-loaded third-party script — GTM, Inside Chat, the Narvar widget, the Google Maps proxy call, and the Adyen Drop-in — is gated by Didomi consent. Each integration document records its own consent posture; the Didomi document is the single contract that all the others honour.

## Cross-cutting principles

- **Fail closed on consent.** If Didomi cannot determine consent state, no third-party tracking or marketing script loads.
- **Fail independently.** One vendor outage must not break the storefront — each integration has a documented degradation path.
- **LCP budget is ≤ 2.0 s at p75 mobile.** Any browser-loaded third-party script defers behind consent or hydration and does not block first paint.
- **Multi-region.** Eight SFCC sites across six regions, eleven active locales. Every integration that varies by region documents the per-storefront configuration matrix.
- **No secrets in the browser bundle.** Public and publishable keys only — anything that grants write access lives server-side, either in MRT environment variables or in SFCC Business Manager.

## Document template

Each integration document follows the same structure for ease of review:

1. Purpose and scope
2. Vendor relationship
3. Browser-side architecture
4. Authentication and credentials
5. Data exchanged
6. Consent and gating
7. Performance and loading strategy
8. Multi-region behaviour
9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
10. Security and privacy
11. Open items requiring client confirmation

Sections may merge where the surface is narrow (for example, the GiveX document folds observability into the security and privacy section) or removed when not applicable.

7	## 1. Purpose & Scope
8	
9	This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.
10	
11	**In scope:**

26	## 2. Solution Overview

28	A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

30	The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

134	## 4. Customisation Model
135	
136	This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's _template extensibility_ model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.
137	
138	All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.
139	
140	**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.
141	
142	**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.
143	
144	### 4.1 Environment Configuration
145	
146	All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. Unless public identifiers, they must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. The table below shows the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised                                       |

Server-side `/payments` calls and HMAC live in SFCC BM                                                                                                                                                                                             | Browser-direct — client key is public by design (PAY-021)                                                                                                                       |
